purpose: Establish that fleet membership, addressing and serving state are discovered from the infrastructure rather than declared in a file that nobody reads. Exists because the measured fleet and the declared fleet disagreed in both directions: the desired-state registry declared two nodes that match nothing, omitted three containers that are running, and pointed at a mesh coordinator whose real name appears in no registry and in no hosts file, while the code looked the coordinator up under the declared name and therefore could not reach a live process.
authority: contracts/observability-facts.json N5 and N6; contracts/observability-loop.json stages 1 and 2.
scope_note: Transverse. Infrastructure discovery and its derivatives, not the network domain. The network is the first adopter, not the owner.

definitions.inventory_of_record: The substrate that can enumerate every machine the fleet runs on, read live. For the containerised fleet this is the hypervisor's container list, not any registry.
definitions.declared_inventory: The set of nodes a registry declares, with their intended addresses and roles.
definitions.observed_inventory: The set of nodes read live from the inventory of record, with their observed hostname, address, role and running services.
definitions.orphan_declaration: A node present in the declared inventory and absent from the observed inventory, whose address resolves nowhere and matches no hostname on any host.
definitions.unregistered_member: A node present in the observed inventory and absent from the declared inventory.
definitions.naming_error: A live node whose observed hostname differs from the name under which the fleet addresses it.

rules.rule: Fleet membership is discovered, not declared. A node joins the fleet by being observed on the inventory of record, not by appearing in a registry.
rules.corollary: A registry may legitimately describe a node that does not exist yet. That is how deployment is planned, and it must be distinguishable from a claim that it exists. Every node entry therefore carries a declared state: planned, deployed, or orphaned.
rules.detection: Read the inventory of record on every observation cycle and diff it against the declared inventory. The diff is a first-class observation, not an error to be raised.
rules.action: Report each difference with the node name, the declared address, and what was actually observed. A planned node that is not observed is reported as planned-and-absent, never as a fault.

rules.rule: A node is addressed by a name that resolves to it. A name that resolves nowhere is a declaration error and must be reportable without operator intervention.
rules.detection: Resolve every node name in both inventories against every resolver the fleet actually uses, including per-host static entries. A name that fails to resolve, or that resolves to a different node than the one declaring it, is a violation.
rules.action: Report the name, the declaring node, and the resolution observed. A fleet whose own mesh coordinator has no resolvable name is in violation of this rule.
rules.established_by: organ-headscale runs as container 100 at 10.10.10.40 with headscale listening on port 8080. The name organ-headscale appears in neither registry and in no hosts file. cynic-node/src/usecases/network_surfaces_uc.rs:564 looks the coordinator up as cynic-lxc-headscale, so its default endpoint cannot find a coordinator that is running.

rules.rule: The runtime registry is a materialisation of the declared inventory on that node, not a second authority. It may lag. The lag is the drift to reconcile and it is measured, never assumed absent.
rules.corollary: The runtime registry and the declared registry must never be held byte-identical, because that makes drift invisible.
rules.detection: Compare the two and emit the difference as an observation carrying both values.
rules.action: Reconcile the runtime toward declared only where observation confirms the node exists; leave the difference visible where it does not.

rules.rule: No fleet name is served from a per-host static file. If a name resolves, it resolves because the authoritative resolver serves it.
rules.detection: Audit every host's static name file for fleet names the declared inventory does not project, and audit the resolver for records that no projection produced.
rules.action: Report both directions. A name in a hosts file with no registry entry, and a registry entry with no served name, are the same class of fault.
rules.established_by: the builder's static name file carries kernel, forgejo, surrealdb, builder and proxmox under synapse.cynic, none of which is served by any zone. dnsmasq answers them with TTL 0 and serves no SOA and no NS for any zone, which is a hosts-file emulation rather than a published zone. service.cynic resolves nowhere, so the six DNS reservations the repository declares name a zone with no published record.

measured_state_at_audit.not_verified: The four non-builder fleet nodes could not be reached: 10.10.10.100 timed out, 10.10.10.101 refused the key. Every observation in this document comes from the builder and from the hypervisor. Whether those nodes agree with any of this is unknown.

detectors_required.detector: read the inventory of record and diff it against declared, emitting orphan declarations and unregistered members
resolve every declared node name against every resolver in use, including static name files
compare declared against runtime registry and emit the drift as an observation
audit static name files on every host against the registry projection

enforcement.natural_owner: cynic-node already exposes a registry-observation surface. Extending it to read the hypervisor and resolve names is the smallest step that makes any of this enforceable.
enforcement.existing_asset: cynic-discovery-host exists and is 220 lines, but it re-exports adapters from the cynic-host monolith rather than owning discovery, which is both a single-owner violation under N6 and an L1 to L1 DAG inversion.
enforcement.blind_spot_summary: Seven blind spots were found by testing these detectors against the current tree. INF9 is the governing one: the detectors have no invocation site, so they are documents. The other six describe what they would miss on the day they run. INF7 and INF8 are the network's own: network actuation performs no read-back, and the domain has no expected-state type, so drift cannot be computed inside it. INF11 bounds every measurement in both contracts: they were taken from one node, and four fleet nodes were unreachable.

explicit_non_goals: discovery does not replace declaration: the declared inventory remains the statement of intent, and INF1 keeps the two distinguishable
this contract does not mandate a discovery protocol such as mDNS or a service mesh; it mandates that membership be read from something that can enumerate it
it does not decide which source wins a disagreement; that is contracts/registry-authority if promoted, or an operator decision

verification.coordinator_running: ssh cynic-builder-ssh 'timeout 8 ssh root@10.10.10.1 "pct exec 100 -- ss -tlnp | grep 8080"'
verification.resolver_nature: ssh cynic-builder-ssh 'dig +short @10.10.10.1 version.bind CHAOS TXT; dig +noall +answer @10.10.10.1 synapse.cynic SOA'

ratification.status: normative on the operator's instruction of 2026-10-05
ratification.promotion_note: written in contracts/ because the operator ruled that a convention which cannot fail a build is prose. The enforcement status is declared above rather than left implicit.

INF5_addressing_is_not_membership.blind_spot: INF1 to INF4 verify NAMES. They never verify ADDRESSES.
INF5_addressing_is_not_membership.measured: 273 literal addresses appear in Rust source, across cynic-protocol, cynic-lifecycle, cynic-host and others. A node can be correctly named and carry a hardcoded address that no longer matches its observed one, and every detector passes.
INF5_addressing_is_not_membership.evidence: grep -rn '10\.10\.10\.\|192\.168\.100\.\|100\.64\.' --include=*.rs crates/ | grep -v target | wc -l  returns 273
INF5_addressing_is_not_membership.detector_required: for every node whose name resolves, resolve it again and compare the returned address against the declared address. Divergence is drift.

INF6_health_is_not_membership.blind_spot: INF1 reads the container inventory, which reports RUNNING. It does not report whether the service inside is healthy, listening, or serving.
INF6_health_is_not_membership.measured: 224 references to service state exist in the codebase, but none is wired to the membership observation. A container that runs and serves nothing satisfies INF1.
INF6_health_is_not_membership.evidence: the mesh coordinator runs as container 100 and listens on 8080, but nothing in the declared inventory asserts that it must listen; conversely a stopped service would satisfy every detector
INF6_health_is_not_membership.detector_required: per declared node, observe the required services and ports. A node that is present and running but not serving is degraded, not healthy.

INF7_no_rollback_proof_on_network_mutati.blind_spot: read_back proof exists widely, 1094 references, but network actuation has none.
INF7_no_rollback_proof_on_network_mutati.measured: crates/cynic-node/src/network_actuator/execution.rs contains zero occurrences of verify, read_back, observe or prove. The DNS bundle writes four files with four independent fs::write calls; a failure on the third leaves a partial state that nothing detects.
INF7_no_rollback_proof_on_network_mutati.detector_required: every network mutation emits a read-back of the state it claims to have produced. A partial write is an observed state, never a silent success.

cross_reference.rfc_sections: RFC-NET-001 §6 lists eight mitigations, none of which is a post-mutation read-back
cross_reference.conflict: the coherence pattern in AGENTS.md requires desired state, observation, reconcile, bounded action, read-back proof. The network implements the first four and stops: actuation reports success without reading the state it produced.
cross_reference.consequence: this is the network's own doctrine breach, not a missing capability elsewhere.

INF8_no_expected_state_in_the_domain.blind_spot: the network domain models what is, never what should be. There is no desired-state type, so drift cannot be computed inside the domain.
INF8_no_expected_state_in_the_domain.measured: grep for desired_state, expected_state or target_state in crates/cynic-network/src returns zero matches. The drift types that exist, ShadowDrift in network_shadow_proof and drift_detected in registry_maintenance, are set by their callers, not computed from an expected state.
INF8_no_expected_state_in_the_domain.evidence: crates/cynic-network/src/registry_maintenance.rs:92 sets drift_detected: false as a literal in a fixture
INF8_no_expected_state_in_the_domain.detector_required: an expected-state type in cynic-network, so that observed minus expected is computable and the domain can emit drift rather than have it supplied.

cross_reference.conflict: principle 3 requires that routing be governed by empirical data rather than hardcoded heuristics, and §4 defines a telemetry snapshot consumed by cynic-storage, cynic-intel and cynic-intel-soc. Both presuppose a comparison between an expected and an observed state. crates/cynic-network has zero desired_state, expected_state or target_state types, so the comparison the RFC relies on cannot be computed inside the domain that owns it.
cross_reference.consequence: RFC-NET-001 §4 is marked partial and this contract names the specific missing piece: not the telemetry, which exists, but the expected state it would be compared against.

INF9_the_detectors_are_dead_code.blind_spot: INF1 to INF4 and the N5 to N7 detectors are declared in contracts and referenced by zero code.
INF9_the_detectors_are_dead_code.measured: the concepts inventory_of_record, orphan_declaration, unregistered_member and declared_state appear in 2 places in the whole workspace, both in tests or documentation, none in a runtime path.
INF9_the_detectors_are_dead_code.detector_required: each detector needs an invocation site. A detector with no caller is a document, not a control.
INF9_the_detectors_are_dead_code.severity_note: this is the most important of the seven. The other six describe what the detectors would miss if they ran. This one says they do not run.

INF10_observation_freshness_is_undefined.blind_spot: nothing defines how old an observation may be before it stops being a fact.
INF10_observation_freshness_is_undefined.measured: 520 timestamps exist across the workspace and 29 in cynic-network, so facts are dated. No contract states a maximum age, so a year-old observation and a one-second-old one are equally trusted.
INF10_observation_freshness_is_undefined.evidence: contracts/observability-loop.json has a staleness rule for thresholds, 30 days, but no freshness bound for observations
INF10_observation_freshness_is_undefined.detector_required: an observation carries a maximum age. Beyond it, the fact degrades to unknown rather than being served as current.

INF11_single_node_visibility.blind_spot: every measurement in these contracts came from one node. Four nodes were unreachable.
INF11_single_node_visibility.measured: 10.10.10.100 timed out, 10.10.10.101 refused the key. A contract written from one vantage point cannot see a split brain: two nodes disagreeing about a fact, or one node holding a private answer.
INF11_single_node_visibility.evidence: the repository itself already has this vocabulary: HealthSignalPayload::NameResolutionInconsistent exists precisely because each node holding a private answer means no node can observe the fault
INF11_single_node_visibility.detector_required: facts that must hold fleet-wide are observed from at least two vantage points and compared. Disagreement is a first-class signal, not a merge.
